replication.target_description: Study 1 / single preregistered replication; 1,020 New York City Airbnb listings; OLS regression of nightly price, with listing/host controls. Confirmatory Model 1, perceived trustworthiness. Located in accepted manuscript pp. 11–12 rather than supplied journal p. 4.

n.sample_role: Airbnb listings used in confirmatory regression; not photo-rating participants
n.exclusions: From 40,227 listings: apartments only; no shared rooms; available at least 30 days in previous year; at least five reviews; verified host identity, available profile photo and only one listing; local rent data required; one clearly visible host face and informative interior apartment photo; 2,110 eligible listings, randomly sampled 1,020. Face++ failures apply to later exploratory model, not this test.
n.quote: Due to resource constraints, we randomly sampled 1,020 listings from the pool of remaining listings. Our analyses are based on this final sample of listings.

reported_success.quote: Our results do not replicate findings by Ert and colleagues (2016; Study 1)

notes: Original table contains several models. Selected separate-trait model matching replication confirmatory analysis (original Model 2 for attractiveness; Model 1 for trustworthiness), rather than interaction-model conditional effects. No metrics converted. Original text obtained from author-uploaded published article on ResearchGate (header DOI 10.1016/j.tourman.2016.01.013), despite landing-page SSRN metadata. Replication source is accepted manuscript dated 19 November 2018, title/authors verified. Input description mentions guests’ choices as well as prices; assigned Study 1 and Table 1 identify the price regression. Guest choices occur in original Study 2 and were not merged into this test. Requested replication unstandardized b is not substituted for the printed β. Authors’ verdict refers to failure to replicate the original Study 1 pattern.
